paragraphs.text: A growing number of popular cities now charge visitors a small tax for each night they stay. In my opinion, this is one of the fairest ways to deal with the pressures that tourism creates.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Residents of these cities pay for the streets to be cleaned, the buses to run and the old buildings to be repaired, yet visitors use all of these services too. A charge of a few euros a night is unlikely to change anyone’s travel plans, but across millions of visitors it can raise large sums.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The difficulty lies in how the money is spent. Too often it disappears into general budgets, and residents see no improvement. I would argue that the income should be clearly linked to projects that tourists and residents can both see.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Some hotel owners fear that the tax will send visitors to cheaper destinations. It is possible that very price-sensitive travellers will choose elsewhere, but the cities with the highest taxes remain among the most visited in the world.
paragraphs.label: D

items.quote: In my opinion, this is one of the fairest ways
items.prompt: The writer considers a nightly tourist tax to be fair.

explanation.en: “In my opinion, this is one of the fairest ways” — the writer calls the tax fair directly → YES.
explanation.kk: «In my opinion, this is one of the fairest ways» — автор салықты тікелей әділ дейді → YES.
explanation.ru: «In my opinion, this is one of the fairest ways» — автор прямо называет налог справедливым → YES.

items.quote: A charge of a few euros a night is unlikely to change anyone’s travel plans
items.prompt: The writer thinks a small nightly charge will persuade many tourists to change their plans.

explanation.en: “unlikely to change anyone’s travel plans” — in the writer’s view a small charge does not change plans → NO.
explanation.kk: «unlikely to change anyone’s travel plans» — автордың ойынша, шағын алым сапар жоспарын өзгертпейді → NO.
explanation.ru: «unlikely to change anyone’s travel plans» — по мнению автора, небольшой сбор планы не меняет → NO.

items.quote: the income should be clearly linked to projects
items.prompt: The writer believes the tax should be the same in every city.

explanation.en: The writer says how the money should be spent, not how large the tax should be in different cities. His view on a single rate is unknown → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Автор ақшаны неге жұмсау керегін айтады, бірақ әр қаладағы салық мөлшері туралы айтпайды. Бірдей мөлшерлеме туралы пікірі белгісіз → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Автор говорит, на что тратить деньги, но не о размере налога в разных городах. Его мнение об одинаковой ставке неизвестно → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: I would argue that the income should be clearly linked to projects that tourists and residents can both see
items.prompt: The writer suggests that the money should pay for projects people can see.

explanation.en: “I would argue that the income should be clearly linked to projects that tourists and residents can both see” — this is the writer’s proposal → YES.
explanation.kk: «I would argue that the income should be clearly linked to projects that tourists and residents can both see» — бұл автордың ұсынысы → YES.
explanation.ru: «I would argue that the income should be clearly linked to projects that tourists and residents can both see» — это предложение автора → YES.

items.quote: It is possible that very price-sensitive travellers will choose elsewhere
items.prompt: The writer accepts that the tax might discourage some travellers.

explanation.en: “It is possible that very price-sensitive travellers will choose elsewhere” — the writer allows that some will go elsewhere. “Accepts … might” = “it is possible” → YES.
explanation.kk: «It is possible that very price-sensitive travellers will choose elsewhere» — автор кейбір туристер басқа жерді таңдауы мүмкін екенін мойындайды. «Accepts … might» = «it is possible» → YES.
explanation.ru: «It is possible that very price-sensitive travellers will choose elsewhere» — автор допускает, что часть туристов уедет в другие места. «Accepts … might» = «it is possible» → YES.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–5. Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in the reading passage? Write YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the claims of the writer, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
